channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: CAPHRA Urges Viet Nam to Choose Regulation Over Prohibition of Nicotine Pouches
item.description: Viet Nam faces a choice between controlling nicotine pouches through regulation or pushing them into a market with no accountability. Prohibition may look decisive, but it rarely removes demand; it usually removes product standards, age controls and consumer protection. A regulated approach would give authorities more oversight while allowing adult smokers access to lower-risk alternatives. Harm reduction is stronger when governments shape the market rather than pretend it can be made to disappear. (Published on August 25, 2026byprlog.org)

item.title: A Flavor Is Not an Age Group
item.description: A flavour is not an age group, and regulation becomes weaker when it treats the two as the same. Adults who smoke often rely on flavoured products because taste can make switching away from cigarettes more acceptable and sustainable. Youth access should be prevented through age checks, retailer enforcement and penalties for illegal sales, not by removing options from adults. Public health needs precision: protect young people without making harm reduction less workable for smokers. (Published on August 25, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Brussels ran a consultation that made the Swedish answer unsayable
item.description: A consultation should make evidence easier to present, not harder to say. Sweden’s experience with low smoking rates and widespread use of smoke-free nicotine products is directly relevant to Europe’s tobacco debate, yet poorly designed questions can push that evidence to the margins. That weakens the process before policy is even written. EU regulation should be open enough to hear what has worked, especially when it challenges the assumptions behind restriction. (Published on August 25, 2026bytheparliamentmagazine.eu)
